subject: Fuaran-Core
$comment: This repository's claims ladder, declared as data in the schema proofs/kit/LADDER.md specifies: what is PROVED, what is only TESTED, what is ASSUMED, and the POLICY the rungs rest on. Each row states what it claims in `statement` and what it does NOT cover in `boundary` (the load-bearing half); its history is the change `phase` cites, never prose here. `claim` is `statement` and `boundary` joined with one space, carried for the registry that still reads `claim`, and held to that join by the ladder family. Authored by hand, never generated, and CHECKED rather than trusted: the Proofs.Ladder family (tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/ProofsLadderTests.fs) holds every row to the tree, and the Proofs.Coverage family (ProofCoverageTests.fs) holds the rows to the shipped surface and pairs every differential to a theorem. A `not claimed` item is the ABSENCE of a row or a row's boundary, never a row at a level that asserts coverage.

claims.statement: Two writes to DIFFERENT slots of one node commute, at every slot a reader of the store can look up, and two slot writes are independent exactly when their slots differ (`slot_writes_independent_iff`) — so the precision the slot clauses buy is sound against a model of what a slot write does. The model is a store of `(slot, value)` bindings, latest first, where a write binds its slot and a read finds the latest binding. Two writes to ONE slot with different values disagree at that slot and the footprint refuses the pair (`same_slot_writes_disagree`); a whole-node write of the slot's node is refused against each of its slots, from either side (`whole_node_refuses_every_slot`).

claims.statement: NO `JVal` CONTAINS A NULL, at any depth — WIRE_FORMAT section 2 rule 4's value half. Stated over the one model here that HAS a null, the foreign document of the read-policy section, so it is a statement and not a tautology: every wire value, viewed as a document, is null-free and reads back as EXACTLY itself under either read policy; the strict reader accepts EXACTLY the null-free documents, an iff; and whatever EITHER reader returns is null-free — the tolerant policy erases an object-member null, it never carries one through. claims.statement: What of the DAG layer remains outside the model. Hashing is abstracted behind an opaque minting function; what it buys is stated separately as `node-ids-distinct`. `Dag.mergeBase` is modelled clause for clause and proved to locate the divergence point for heads whose lanes hang off one merged node (`merge-base-divergence`), and over ANY two heads, a criss-cross merge included: it returns a common ancestor no other common ancestor descends from, or refuses exactly over disjoint histories (`merge-base-maximal`). Production's current `deepest` is modelled too (`merge-base-as-it-runs`), and so are `commonBase` over N heads, the index's own four queries and `cut`'s kept set. The index's queries are modelled over its slots under the SLOT-AGREEMENT abstraction: a slot's bitset is read as the set of ids whose bits it sets, `Count[s]` as that set's size, a scan over slot positions as a pass over the set, and the index's order array as the whole DAG's drain, the order `Reach.ofDag` builds. The ancestor closure, the difference against the base's closure, the lookup and the fold built on them are not assumed at either shape: see `dag-delta-recovery`, `fold-from-the-dag`, `dag-delta-recovery-merged-head` and `fold-from-a-merged-dag`.
claims.boundary: Outside the model: the hashing itself; the recovery of a delta that itself contains a two-parent node, which is no spine and has no append order to be identified with; the word layout under the slot-agreement reading; and `Reach.extend`'s splice of a new leaf into the order, which `Conformance.reachLaws` samples. WHICH maximal common ancestor `Dag.mergeBase` returns is the (closure size, id) tie-break, a policy and not a fact, and a deterministic function of the two closures.

claims.statement: The signed head binds the chain it seals: two linear chains that both verify from one genesis, and whose heads both verify under ONE attestation, are the same chain — the same records, so the same ops in the same order. It is the composition of two facts. The attestation verifies against at most one head (`signature_binds`, the row `signature-binds-one-head` below), and a verified chain's head determines the chain: `same_head_same_chain_from` is the linear chain's own injectivity, walked tip to root, spending `rec_injective_on` — the DERIVED composite (`chain-envelope-parse`) — once per record, with a chain told apart from its own extensions by the sequence number in the pre-image. `signed_sentinel_covers_the_empty_chain` states the other side, that under a signed sentinel the empty chain is accepted under every genesis. Proved with no assume and no admit under --report_assumes error.
claims.boundary: Both chains carry actors the code emits and a re-minted splice carries the condition on its steps. It carries one boundary as a premise rather than hiding it: `OpStream.head` returns the literal empty string for the empty chain (not `cfg.Genesis`), so the theorem asks that the signed head is not that sentinel, which is a condition on the one head being verified and one a verifier can check. What it deliberately is not: a claim about any signature algorithm, key custody or a keyring's lockout rules, and not UNFORGEABILITY — the theorem is about the one original attestation, and that nobody can mint a second one over a rewritten head is the signature scheme's own claim. Nothing is stated over a compacted stream: `compact` trusts the boundary hash it reads, so a signed head over a compaction binds the discarded prefix only under `compact-preserves-verify`'s premise.

claims.statement: Replace, insert or drop ONE op and RE-MINT the whole chain from genesis, so that `verifyChain` accepts the result, and it is still refused under the original attestation. The re-mint is the point: it is the rewrite `chain-tamper-detected` cannot see, because it produces a perfectly intact chain, and it is the forgery `Conformance.attestationLaws` builds with its own rehash. One theorem over a three-case `splice`, guarded by `splice_changes` — a replacement by a different step at an index the chain has, any insertion, a removal at an index the chain has. `signed_head_rejects_rewrite` is the general form beside it: ANY chain other than the one that was signed is refused, however intact.
claims.boundary: A splice that changes nothing re-mints the signed chain itself and is rightly accepted, which is what the `splice_changes` guard excludes. Same premises as `signed-head-binds-chain`, of which both are corollaries.

claims.statement: The signature primitive, abstract, with ONE assumed property: an attestation verifies against at most one head — `verify` holds only for the signed bytes. It is an explicit lemma-valued PARAMETER (`signature_binds`) of the two signed-head theorems rather than an assume, so which results depend on it is visible in their signatures. It is BINDING and not unforgeability: a sink whose `Verify` compares the attestation's recorded `Head` has it by construction, and what the cryptography buys is the half no row here states.
claims.boundary: Core ships no signer (`OpStream.noAttestation` signs nothing and verifies nothing) and the only concrete sinks in this repository are test-local, so the model's abstract `verify` is bridged to no production signature at all: that is the bridge this row names. It is `unscheduled` rather than `permanent` because something COULD close it, and it is already half-built — the property is one a host's `IAttestationSink` either has or lacks (a sink that verifies everything falsifies it), and the shipped kit samples it at the host's own sink: `Conformance.attestationLaws`' prefix arm and its two rehashed-forgery arms are each one attestation offered two heads. Recording it as a `domain-obligation` discharged by that law is what would close it, and it is not done, because the discharge relation is shipped data (`Fuaran.Core.Families.obligations`, held to this file row for row by the Conformance.Families family), so adding the pair is a change to a shipped package's source rather than a proof-leg artefact, and is an operator's call. Under the `noAttestation` default these theorems say nothing, which is correct — there is no signed head.

claims.statement: The extracted model agrees with OpStream.head, attestHead, verifyAttestation and the verifyChain-and-verifyAttestation composition over generated chains from two witnesses, generated KEYRINGS, and every replace / insert / drop splice of each chain followed by a full re-mint — beside the `IAttestationSink` SEAM driven by a test-local keyring sink. The sink's `Verify` deliberately does not compare the attestation's recorded head, so binding is spent on the keyed digest rather than satisfied by construction. Each splice is spelled twice and independently, as the model's `splice` and as a plain list edit of production's steps, and the two must mint the same records; `splice_changes` must agree with whether production's steps moved. Beside the model-against-production comparison, PRODUCTION is held to `signed_head_rejects_splice` on its own verdict: every re-minted splice must pass verifyChain (or it is not the rewrite the theorem is about) and must be refused under the original attestation. Vacuity guards require a signed chain, a multi-key ring, a verifier lacking the key, a re-labelled attestation, a refused splice of each of the three kinds, an accepted no-op splice, and every in-place tamper refused. Three further cases: a model handed a different hash must disagree; under a sink that verifies EVERYTHING the re-minted splice is ACCEPTED, by production and by the model alike, so `signature_binds` is observed load-bearing; and the empty-chain sentinel measured on production. The differential was also reddened by hand before it was trusted, by two perturbations of the extracted oracle — a head read from the first record rather than the last, and a drop that drops nothing — each of which failed the generated cases.
claims.boundary: Agreement is over those pools, never over all inputs. Core ships no production signer, so the seam is exercised only through a test-local keyring sink and the differential claims no production signer it cannot reach.

claims.statement: The recursive-descent JSON parser reaches exactly one outcome on every input — an accepted value or a CLASSIFIED refusal, never both and never neither. That it is Tot at all is the content rather than a formality: F* admits the mutual group only after showing it terminates on every input, and a recursive-descent parser over a mutable index has no syntactic reason to. Every consuming sub-parser carries the remaining input's strict decrease in its RETURN TYPE, and that refinement is the whole termination argument.

The id-witness axiom is named here too, because it is the witness law every id-equality theorem consumes: every model reads an id through ONE decidable equality — `TreeOps` and `Preservation` take ids as their key strings, the form `IdWitness.ToString` writes every address in, compared with `=` — while production keys `ToString` in `wellFormed` / `footprint` / `Tree.Index` and calls `Equals` in `tryFind` / `updateNode`. The theorems transfer to a domain's `'Id` exactly when the two agree: `id_key_faithful idw.Equals idw.ToString` (`Equals a b <==> ToString a = ToString b`), defined in `TreeOps.fst` section 0.
claims.boundary: A domain's own `ReplaceChildren` is that domain's promise, sampled by the conformance pack and proved by nothing; where it does not hold, every theorem above is about a different function from the one that runs. The pack's own boundary: `witnessLaws` exempts a leaf from the round trip, so a witness whose `ReplaceChildren` is partial on leaves is lawful. A domain whose `Equals` and `ToString` disagree runs a different algebra from the one proved; `witnessLaws`' identities cell samples exactly that relation, over drawn pairs and over pairs built to share a key, so the law covers the axiom the models consume rather than only reflexivity and the round trip — by sampling, not proof.

claims.statement: That the witness surface is the whole of the tree. `Tree.ids` walks `NodeWitness.Children`, so a node a domain holds in a keyed, non-structural position is invisible to the uniqueness scan, to every theorem above, and to the differential. Stated as an assumption rather than a limitation because it is what the theorems quantify over: they are true of the witness view, and the witness view is what `Ops` can see. A domain that hands its `KeyedWitness` to `Ops.applyContainedKeyed` gets the `DuplicateId` refusal over the keyed walk from Core (`keyed-apply-preserves-wf`), so what is left of the obligation is the DECLARATION — that `KeyedChildren` reports every keyed position the domain's own walk sees, and that `ReplaceKeyedChildren` and `ReplaceChildren` leave each other's positions alone. `Conformance.keyedApplyLaws` certifies exactly that: its agreement law holds the engine's refusal to the domain's own check over collisions BUILT through `PlaceKeyedChild`, and its witness laws hold the two rebuilds apart.
claims.boundary: The unkeyed `Ops` forms still see exactly what `Children` reports, and a domain that does not use the keyed forms keeps uniqueness over its keyed positions as its own obligation, with `Conformance.keyedChildrenLaws` certifying the domain's own full-walk id check against its declaration. The row is marked `domain-declared` because the law checks the declaration and cannot check past it: `keyedApplyLaws` holds the engine to what `KeyedChildren` REPORTS, so a domain with keyed positions that declares none passes it by declaration. A green run says the declaration is consistent; only the domain can say it is complete — so this row is not DISCHARGED by the law it names, it is checked against the domain's own word.

The located half is a DISJUNCTION, which is content rather than a weakening: there are two capability sites and they name nodes in two different places — the (new) PARENT, a node of the tree, and an interior node of the SUBTREE an `InsertChild` carries, which the duplicate-id scan guarantees is NOT in the tree; a single tree lookup would be false of the second site.
claims.boundary: It deliberately does NOT say the capability only adds a refusal: it can PRE-EMPT another one. claims.statement: The extracted container model agrees with the shipped `Ops.applyContained` and `Ops.canApplyContained` over a GENERATED `canHold` — a random subset of the pool's kind vocabulary per trial, including the empty predicate (nothing can hold children) and the total one (where the engine is `apply` again), all eight drawn. Five comparisons per probe: the verdict and the accepted result through production's own `Tree.encodeHash`, the rejection by class, the dry run against the mutating call on each side, `applyContained` against `apply` on production, and the invariant asserted on production wherever its hypothesis is met. Adequacy is counted per capability SITE — insert refusals, move refusals, batch inheritance, graft refusals and pre-emptions separately — because a run that reached only the insert site could not catch the go-red, which is a move. The go-red is the model's own instrument: an engine checking the capability on insert and not on move, proved in F* to admit a move the real one refuses, required to lose here. The GRAFT site is reached by construction: a leaf graft can never carry an interior offender, so the probes mint a graft whose root holds a child in both a container kind and a leaf kind, and both verdicts arise within one run. Measured at 30 trials, seed 1400: 1,245 accepted, 1,305 refused, 649 insert refusals of which 124 are the graft site, 370 move refusals, 112 batch inheritances, 89 pre-emptions, the invariant asserted on 1,028 probes.
claims.boundary: Agreement is over the pool drawn, never over all inputs. The predicate is drawn because a differential run against one hand-picked predicate would certify that instance and nothing about the quantifier the theorems carry.

claims.statement: THE TWO MODELS OF THE SAME LANGUAGE AGREE. On every byte sequence `Canonical.write Rendering.CrossHost` emits, in every trailing context the grammar produces, theorem 7's reader and theorem 4's parser both ACCEPT — neither refuses — and return the SAME value and the SAME remainder, up to the correspondence between the two models' types. It relates a reader proved to exist and invert the encoder to the parser model (`JsonParse.parse`; in production, `Json.read` at no bound but the cap), proved total with its refusals classified, so the round trip a consumer performs is proved rather than only measured by the differential over the corpus. It is a BRIDGE and not a model: nothing new is modelled, neither grammar is widened, and both readers are the ones their own models define. The two models share no type — `pc` is the alphabet correspondence and `pv` the value correspondence, which is not an identity in three places, each a modelling decision already taken (a numeral comes back as its TOKEN, a string as the `och` list `parseString` builds, an object's keys in that same form). It holds under BOTH null policies, which is the half that is easy to miss: theorem 1's member-null fork can only fire on a member whose value begins with `n`, and `render_head_dispatches` proves no rendering does — `parse_render_is_policy_independent` is that corollary. `pc` carries NO `bridged` hypothesis, deliberately: `bridged` is the faithfulness condition for a HOST's mapping, and `pc` sends a `CPlain` carrying a reserved spelling to `COther` of it rather than to the constructor that spelling names, so the theorem holds of every value.

claims.statement: The numerals are OPAQUE, as they are for the decode combinators and for the parser, and for the same reason: the F# extraction carries no floats and F*'s integers are unbounded where `JInt` is Int32. The two layouts and the numeral read-back are parameters, and the ONE premise the canonical-form theorems carry about them is that the read-back inverts the layouts (`tok_read_ok`) — which is the property `Double.ToString("R")` is DEFINED by, since rule 5 pins the float layout as the shortest digit sequence that round-trips. Rule 5's injectivity lemmas are DERIVED from that premise rather than assumed beside it, because a read-back that is a function cannot return two different values for one token. One lemma, `no-null-rendered`, carries a SECOND and WEAKER premise about the same parameters — `layouts_numeric`, that every character of both layouts is a numeral character — because it speaks of every value, including the integral floats outside the canonical subset about whose layout `tok_read_ok` is silent. The two BRIDGE rows — `canon-parser-agreement` and `canonical-parse-roundtrip` — carry a THIRD premise about the same two layouts, `numerals_bridge`, and it is this row's because it is the same opacity seen from the other side: theorem 4 takes `System.Double.TryParse`'s verdict as its own parameter (`parser-float-readback-opaque`), so a bridge between two opaque parameters can only relate them. It says each layout begins with a character the parser's value dispatch sends to `parseNumber`, and that in every trailing context the grammar produces `parseNumber` scans back exactly the token the encoder emitted and classifies it on the constructor rule 5 chose. It is exhibited SATISFIABLE rather than assumed consistent — `numerals_bridge_is_satisfiable` runs `parseNumber` on a concrete wire's two layouts in every such context — because a premise about two parameters at once is the shape that can be contradictory without looking it, and a contradictory premise would make both bridge rows true and worthless.
claims.boundary: Nothing is said about the digits themselves: which decimal .NET produces for a given double is measured by the differential and by the cross-host parity vectors, not proved; `numerals_bridge` likewise says nothing about which digits either layout produces. `layouts_numeric` binds `no-null-rendered` alone and `numerals_bridge` the two bridge rows alone; the canonical-form theorems still carry exactly one premise.

claims.statement: The F* BACKEND is certified over the vocabularies the engine is certified on, and the models it emits are total. `proofs/Vocabulary.fst`, `DocVocabulary.fst` and `ScoreVocabulary.fst` carry the types, the discriminated encoder and the tag-dispatch decoder of the engine's reference vocabulary (`tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/ReferenceIdl.fs`) and of the two vendored non-UI samples, emitted by a fourth backend of the IDL's code generator (`FStarTarget`, beside the F# structural layer, the TypeScript encoder and the JSON schema) over the `jval` model and the combinators modelled with it — the same certification set `IdlCertificationTests` holds the F# and TypeScript backends to, reaching both declared wire shapes and every type case the reference vocabulary was authored to reach. Every decoder is `Tot` on an arbitrary `jval` and therefore total and terminating on every input, which F* admits only after proving it; the termination argument is `get_prop`'s return-type refinement, since a decoder that descends BY NAME into a value it looked up has no syntactic one. Generic unions are monomorphised at the arguments each vocabulary reaches, which keeps every definition first-order. Proved with no assume and no admit under --report_assumes error. Every kind other than the refused ones is modelled: `FStarTarget.proofKinds`, the UI-scale cost control, is deliberately not what selects here (over the reference vocabulary it keeps one kind of five, which is pinned), because the whole set costs seconds. Each committed file is held to a fresh generation from its vocabulary IN THE TEST PROJECT by the Proofs.Vocabulary family — a vocabulary that moves without a regeneration fails the leg as vocabulary drift, and nothing in the leg reads the shared corpus for these files. Over these models the ROUND TRIP (`dec_node (enc_node x) == Ok x`, `rt_node` in `VocabularyProofs.fst` / `DocVocabularyProofs.fst` / `ScoreVocabularyProofs.fst`) is emitted by the same walk, committed, and carried as its own `proved` rows (`vocabulary-round-trip`, `doc-vocabulary-round-trip`, `score-vocabulary-round-trip`). It is emitted ONE LEMMA PER CONSTRUCTOR over a LINEAR presence split — by MEMBER, one `lk_…` lookup per member with the other conditional members left free, `2k + r'` lemmas for a constructor with k of them, where a per-pattern split is 2^k in the lemma COUNT (`fuaran#1754` measured that at 71,722 lemmas in a 114 MB script) — and discharges at the leg's own rlimit of 40 under `--quake 3`. claims.boundary: What is proved is the BACKEND, not the UI vocabulary: the UI vocabulary's model, proofs, cost and exhaustive-coverage decision are the adopter's — `fuaran#1754`, the kit's first adopter — where the cost is charged to the commits that change UI kinds, a domain's proof in the substrate's CI being the placement D14 rules out. ONE refusal shape is met, and it is named rather than dropped, because a silently-dropped member would make the round trip a theorem about a document nobody sends: a declared NUMERIC default has no F* literal when the numeric carriers are opaque type parameters, so `Measure` (reference), `Note` and `Chord` (score) are refused by name in their headers — the same class as `Tabs.activeIndex` — and `IdlFStarTargetTests` pins the set as exactly those three and pins every other refusal class of the backend to a hand-written case. What the linear split does NOT fix is named where it is measured (`proofs/README.md`): the encoder's own emitted TEXT is 2^k, so at sixteen conditional members the MODEL cannot be checked at all, and a negative lookup still walks the conditional tail — both belong to the model emitter, not to the proof shape. The one fact about its output the agreement theorems need — `Order` holds no id twice — is proved through a CHECKER: `Propagation.validTopo` (Order distinct; Order and the cycles' members partition the map's ids; every read of an Order id the map holds appears earlier or lies in a cycle) is modelled clause for clause as `valid_topo`, an order it accepts is PROVED duplicate-free (`valid_topo_distinct`, row `propagation-topo-certificate`), and the agreement theorem holds of any order it accepts whatever produced it (`evalfrom_agrees_certified`). claims.statement: A PLACED INSERT IS ONE INSERT PLUS AT MOST ONE REORDER. `TreePlacement.place`'s script once the position `k` is resolved — `[InsertChild(parent, node)]` when `k` is the parent's child count, else `[Batch [InsertChild(parent, node); ReorderChildren(parent, List.insertAt k (id node) (ids cs))]]` — is modelled as `place_script`, and on every WELL-FORMED tree, with the parent present, the insert's own uniqueness clause passing (`first_dup n t = None`, the check `InsertChild` makes) and `k <= length cs`, `apply_all` of it is `Ok (ins_at p k n t)`: the tree whose parent's children are `insertAt k n cs` and in which nothing else has changed (`placed_insert_is_insert_plus_reorder`). So the reorder leg is always accepted, lands the node exactly at position `k`, and moves no other child and touches no other node. `place_at_end_is_bare_insert` is the end case alone (the script IS the single insert), `reorder_leg_is_not_identity` its converse (at every earlier position the wanted order differs from the appended one, so the reorder leg is dropped exactly when it would be the identity), and `placement_lands_at_position` pins the zero-based reading by evaluation.
claims.boundary: Holds only on a well-formed tree with the parent present, the uniqueness clause passing and `k <= length cs`. claims.statement: A COMPACTED STREAM KEEPS WRITING. For every stream, reducer, hash and snapshot payload, every boundary n and the (snapshot, tail) that compact produces at n, the compaction of the APPENDED stream is the appended compaction — `compact (append_full rs a o) n == Compacted snap (append_to snap tail a o)`, snapshot and tail alike — so the record `OpStream.Compacted.appendTo` mints onto the tail is the record `append` mints onto the whole stream: at sequence `snap.Seq + length tail` and linked to the tail's last hash or, on an EMPTY tail, to the snapshot's boundary hash. With it (`compact_preserves_verify` on the appended stream) the appended original verifies exactly when its discarded prefix verifies and the appended compaction verifies across, and `append_after_compact_verifies_iff` is the chartered sentence with its premise: over a prefix that verified, `verifyChain (rs @ [r]) = verifyAcross snap (appendTo snap tail r)`. Proved with no assume and no admit.
claims.boundary: The verification equation holds only over a prefix that verified. claims.statement: RE-COMPACTION IS COMPACTION. Compacting a compacted stream again k records past its boundary n — `compact_from snap tail k`, the model of `OpStream.Compacted.compactFrom` at `atSeq = n + k` — is compacting the full stream at n + k: the same snapshot (sequence, state, boundary hash and seal, in the snapshot's own payload) and the same tail, or the same refusal with the same message, for every stream, reducer, hash and payload. A prefix refusal is reported at the ORIGIN index, because the cut records are replayed numbered from the snapshot's boundary, exactly as `compact` numbers them. Proved with no assume and no admit.

claims.statement: THE KEY INDEX SURVIVES COMPACTION. The first-wins key-index fold splits at ANY boundary: the index of the first n records, continued over the rest, is the index of the whole stream (`key_index_rebuild_parity`), and at a compaction `compact` produced, the discarded prefix's index (`Compacted.Keys`) continued over the tail is `KeyIndex.ofStream` of the uncompacted stream (`key_index_compact_parity`). So `OpStream.Compacted.keyIndex` answers every key the stream ever produced, with the entry it first produced, and an idempotent retry of a pre-compaction key is the `Duplicate` it was before the compaction. Proved with no assume and no admit.
claims.boundary: NOT claimed: the persistence of `Keys`, which no hash binds and which the host carries beside the compacted stream (DECISIONS, the `fuaran-core#301` entry).

claims.statement: REPLAY OF A RECORDED SESSION IS THE SESSION. STRICT replay (`OpStream.replayEffectStrict`, modelled before the domain decode as `replay_strict`) of a recorded session over its own complete journal answers every value the session realised, in order, and leaves nothing in the journal (`replay_record` — `replay (record s) = s`): a non-deterministic effect from its capture, a deterministic one from the live source. Beside it, `truncated_journal_exhausted`: the same session replayed against a journal that lacks the capture of its LAST non-deterministic effect stops `Exhausted`, naming that effect — the tail truncation the lenient `replayEffect` answers from the live source with no signal. Proved with no assume and no admit.
claims.boundary: Given only that every label is canonical. NOT claimed: the domain decode, a round trip the value codec owns (the theorem says the decoder is handed the recorded encoding); the label vocabulary itself (`isDeterminismLabel` is a parameter, held equal to `Effect.tryDeterminismOfTag` by a test); and a truncation the session never reaches, which only an anchored head (`verifyCapturesAt`) detects.
